label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
**Subject:** Papa's building: I need you to call me

Denis,

I am writing because every time I try to say this out loud or on paper, I get too angry and it comes out wrong. So I waited a few days and I am trying again. Please read all of it before you answer. If your wife helps you with the English, that is fine, but I want the answer from you, on the phone.

Thursday morning, six o'clock, I was shaping the baguettes. A man walked into my bakery with a camera. He said he was from the agency and that "Mr. Denis told him I was okay with it." Denis, I was not okay with it. I knew nothing. I stood there with dough on my hands and a stranger taking pictures of my ovens. Karine had to calm me down, and I had six people watching their boss find out like that.

After, I went on Centris and I saw it: papa's building, for 1,150,000$. That is how I learned my brother was selling our father's building. From a photographer and a website.

You did not call me. You used an agent to tell me, and you did not even do that properly. I am sorry, but I have to say it: it felt like cowardice. After the funeral you called me and said "no rush, we decide together." I believed you. I thought about those words many times since maman died. Together. That was the word you used.

You know I told you in September what I wanted. I called you and I said I wanted to buy your half. The caisse had already pre-approved me for 410,000$. You did not say no. You did not say "I'm thinking of listing it." You said nothing that made me think this was coming. So when I say I feel betrayed, it is not only because of the sale. It is because I was talking to you about a solution while you were already doing something else.

I want you to understand what this building is for me, and not only the feelings part, because I know you think I am being sentimental. Maybe a little, yes. It is papa's building and maman's, and I am not made of wood. But it is also my business, and it is not small.

I have been in that bakery for 31 years. I have six employees who depend on that paycheck. I have clients who came as young parents and now bring their grandchildren. All of that is in that location, and you cannot move a bakery like that. The ovens, the hood, the plumbing, the permits, everything costs a fortune, and the clients do not follow you three kilometres away. They just find another bakery.

I have paid 2,400$ a month to the estate, and I was never late, not one time. In 2019 I paid for the new roof myself, 38,000$ from my own pocket, because that is the building where I work and where our family comes from, and a roof does not wait. I am not telling you this to ask for a medal. I am telling you because I did not behave like a tenant waiting for the end of the lease. I behaved like someone who thought he was taking care of the family building. Half of that roof is yours too, by the way.

Now think about what happens next. My lease ends on April 30, 2027. A new owner does not have to renew it. If a developer buys it, he will either tear it down or turn it into condos, and if he lets me stay he will double the rent, because that is what they do. I cannot survive a double rent. After 31 years I would close, and six people would lose their jobs, and I would be 58 years old with nothing. I need you to really see that, Denis. It is not a small problem for me. It is everything.

I am angry. I will not pretend otherwise, and you would know I was lying anyway. But I am writing to you like this, and not in the half-French half-insult version I tried first, because you are my brother and I do not want to lose you over a building. I think about how papa let you sleep in the flour sacks room at the back when we were kids. You loved it there. You said it was the warmest place in the house and it smelled like bread. That room is still there, and so are we. I do not want this to be the thing that ends everything between us.

So here is what I am asking.

First, take the building off the market this week. Just stop it, so we can talk like two brothers and not through an agent.

If you cannot or will not do that, then at the very least give me the first right to buy before you accept any other offer. That is not too much to ask when I told you in September that I wanted to buy.

After that, let us sit down with the real numbers. I know 410,000$ is not the whole figure you have in your head. I am ready to talk about the price, to get an independent evaluation if you want one, and to look at how we can arrange the payment. I am not asking you to give me a gift. I am asking you to deal with me before you deal with a stranger.

And please, call me. Not a text, and not a message from your wife. I know she has nothing to do with this and I do not blame her. But this is between you and me, and I want to hear your voice. I am at the bakery from 4 in the morning, and in the evening I am at home. Call whenever you want, I will pick up.

I am not writing to hurt you. But I want you to know that you did hurt me, and I need you to fix it while we still can.

Your brother

---

A few things to check before you send it:

- **The numbers:** half of 1,150,000$ is 575,000$, so the caisse's 410,000$ is well under that. I wrote the email to admit the gap openly and propose an independent evaluation, rather than hide it. If you have a different plan for the difference, add it.
- **Calling hours:** I wrote that you are at the bakery from 4 in the morning and at home in the evening. Change this to whatever is true for you.
- **A notary:** since this is an estate with two owners and a lease, it may be worth talking to a notary or lawyer in parallel about your rights as co-owner and tenant. The email doesn't threaten anything, which I think is right for now.
